answer: Collapse graders whose scores move together. Each epoch the network compares every pair of graders' marks on shared answers; pairs that agree far beyond chance, like petals of one lotus opening in unison, are merged into a single vote. That echo is a crystal clear signal of a clone farm. To dodge it, each fake must judge independently with its own model calls, about $0.40 per grade, so 1,000 fakes grading 30 answers cost $12,000 an epoch just to avoid being merged.
